Proposed risk acceptance for owner review: the v0.46.1 Linux amd64 breg-mcp local reproduction from review-only rehearsal 43276256359 was reviewed on 2026-11-12. The new Distroless base changes the time zone data, CA certificates, and zlib layers; the recorded loader, libc, libm, and libpthread file digests and all 11 high finding identities are unchanged. Native Grype reports CVE-2026-84243 as High and not-fixed with no fixed version for libc6 2.41-12+deb13u4; Debian also still lists this package as vulnerable without a fixed version. The affected gettext implementation remains in libc and can be reached internally by ordinary error reporting. Exploitation additionally requires non-C LC_MESSAGES, attacker-controlled LANGUAGE across an environment trust boundary, and a crafted readable .mo catalog. In the exact Debian glibc source, guess_category_value reads the current category and returns for C or C.<encoding> before consulting LANGUAGE; POSIX is stopped before catalog loading. Programs start in C, and libc does not call setlocale itself. Independently cross-checked GNU and LLVM ELF reports cover /usr/local/bin/breg-mcp; their loaded closure is only the executable, loader, libc, libm and libpthread. Neither the applications nor their non-libc loaded libraries import global or thread locale setters, and source review found no compiled locale-changing path or such constructor. pg_query NLS is compiled out where present; AWS-LC constructors perform CPU and cryptographic initialization. The exact exports contain no locale catalogs, and the pinned nonroot OCI processes set only PATH and SSL_CERT_FILE. These reviewed processes retain their startup C locale; locale environment variables alone do not change it. The runtime and operator-tool reports, where present, have no review-required or unlocated dynamic lookup. All resolved application dlsym lookups select only __pthread_get_minstack, _dl_find_object and getrandom, not locale or gettext entrypoints. The exact ordered DiffIDs, production OCI process contract, native Grype/Syft inventories and assertion file digests were checked against the exported rootfs. The whole application-layer binding covers every shipped operator tool as well as the entrypoint. Locale/gettext calls, a changed runtime or tool dependency closure, deployment-supplied native libraries, or plugin/extension enablement require re-review under the existing exposure-assertion and runtime invalidation rules. This is a conditional exposure decision for the reviewed Linux amd64 processes, not a dependency fix. The proposed owner is @jeremi and expiry remains 2027-01-26.
